prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- Hundreds of people filled a college auditorium Wednesday to pay their last respects to an El Reno, Oklahoma, woman slain along with her four children last week. Summer Rust's children -- clockwise from top, Autumn, Kirsten, Evynn and Teagin -- carve pumpkins. About 300 people attended the service at Redlands Community College for Summer Rust, 25; her son, Teagin, 4; and daughters Evynn, 3, and Autumn and Kirsten, both 7, CNN affiliate KOCO reported. Rust's white coffin was placed in front of the podium, flanked by the smaller caskets carrying her children. Each casket had a picture of the victim, surrounded by flowers. A slide show of the family played on an overhead screen throughout the service. "I've preached a lot of funerals, but none like this one," said the Rev. Gerald Van Horn. "This has been on my heart ever since I heard about it. I first learned of it from the news, and I said, 'In El Reno? No way.' ... We don't have to deal with tragedy very often, but it has come, and the reality of it has sunk in. Searching my heart on what to say, I have found it difficult." He told mourners that God is near and feels their pain but acknowledged that Rust and her children "will be greatly missed." The bodies were found January 12 in Rust's apartment in El Reno, about 30 miles west of Oklahoma City. According to the document, each of the victims was suffocated and strangled. Crime scene investigators said each body had ligature marks around the neck. Rust's boyfriend, Joshua Steven Durcho, 25, admitted choking her to death but said the children were not there at the time, according to an affidavit filed last week. He was arrested in Hamilton County, Texas, officials said. A spokeswoman at the Canadian County, Oklahoma, Sheriff's Office said Durcho was being held in the county jail after waiving extradition. Durcho's cousin found Rust's body and called officers, who found the children's bodies in the apartment, says an affidavit written by a special agent with the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation. An apparent acquaintance of Durcho's told police he came to her apartment Monday afternoon and told her he had "choked" Summer Rust to death and he was leaving Oklahoma, according to the affidavit. The affidavit says Durcho told the woman "that the children were at their grandmother's residence ... while he and Summer worked out their relationship problems." Rust's mother, Susan Rust of Carson City, Nevada, said Durcho was unemployed and had been living with Rust and her children. Authorities in Texas said Durcho was arrested after a state trooper attempted to stop his car because the trooper suspected that the driver was drunk. When the trooper ran the license plate on the car, it matched the tag number of a vehicle sought by Oklahoma police.

The memorial was held for 25-year-old Summer Rust; her 4-year-old son, Teagin; her 3-year-old daughter, Evynn; and her 7-year-old daughters, Autumn and Kirsten. In one family photograph, the children—Autumn, Kirsten, Evynn and Teagin, shown clockwise from the top—are carving pumpkins.

Rust’s white coffin stood before the auditorium podium, with her children’s smaller caskets arranged beside it. Flowers and a photograph of each victim adorned the coffins, while images of the family were projected on a screen throughout the ceremony.

The Rev. Gerald Van Horn said that, despite having conducted many funerals, he had never faced one like this. He recalled learning about the deaths through the news and reacting with disbelief that such a tragedy had occurred in El Reno. He told those attending that the reality of the loss had settled over the community and that he had struggled to find the right words. Van Horn assured the mourners that God was close to them and shared in their suffering, while recognizing that Rust and her children would be deeply missed.

The five bodies were discovered January 12 inside Rust’s apartment in El Reno, approximately 30 miles west of Oklahoma City. Investigators reported that all five victims had been strangled and suffocated, and each had ligature marks around the neck.

An affidavit filed the previous week said Rust’s boyfriend, 25-year-old Joshua Steven Durcho, confessed to choking Rust to death but claimed the children were elsewhere at the time. Officials said he was arrested in Hamilton County, Texas. After giving up his right to extradition proceedings, Durcho was being detained in the Canadian County, Oklahoma, jail, according to a sheriff’s office spokeswoman.

A special agent with the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation wrote in an affidavit that Durcho’s cousin discovered Rust’s body and contacted authorities. Officers then located the bodies of the four children elsewhere in the apartment.

The affidavit also described a statement from a woman who apparently knew Durcho. She told police that he arrived at her apartment Monday afternoon, said he had “choked” Rust to death and announced that he planned to leave Oklahoma. According to the document, Durcho told her the children were staying at their grandmother’s home while he and Rust attempted to resolve problems in their relationship.

Rust’s mother, Susan Rust of Carson City, Nevada, said Durcho did not have a job and had been residing with her daughter and the children.

Texas authorities said a state trooper apprehended Durcho after trying to pull over his vehicle on suspicion that the driver was intoxicated. A check of the license plate showed that it matched the tag number of a vehicle Oklahoma law enforcement officers were seeking.

**Five members of Oklahoma family remembered at emotional funeral**

**EL RENO, Oklahoma (CNN)** — Hundreds of mourners gathered in El Reno to remember 25-year-old Summer Rust and her four young children, whose deaths stunned this small community west of Oklahoma City.

Five caskets stood at the front of the church during the service, surrounded by flowers, family photographs and other reminders of the children’s short lives. Clergy members offered prayers and words of comfort as relatives and friends remembered Rust as a devoted mother and the children as energetic and loving.

Rust and her children, all between 3 and 7 years old, were found dead inside their El Reno apartment in January 2009. Authorities said the five had been strangled. Police went to the home after concerned relatives were unable to reach the family.

Investigators quickly began searching for Rust’s boyfriend, Joshua Steven Durcho, who had been living at the apartment. Durcho was arrested in Texas after authorities found him following a crash involving Rust’s vehicle. He was returned to Oklahoma and charged with five counts of first-degree murder.

Officials did not publicly identify a motive at the time. Prosecutors said each death constituted a separate murder charge, while Durcho was entitled to the presumption of innocence unless proved guilty in court.

The funeral brought much of El Reno together in grief. Community members donated money, food and services to help the victims’ relatives, while counselors were made available to children and families struggling with the loss.

As the service ended, mourners filed past the five caskets — one for a mother and four for children whose lives, speakers said, ended far too soon.
